source_snapshot.items: Check BMC firmware version via ipmitool mc info
source_snapshot.procedure: Run `ipmitool mc info`; says Firmware Revision is the first two bytes of the firmware number, then says the first byte is the third byte of the firmware number.
source_snapshot.criteria: Result is correct and command works without error.
source_snapshot.script: No Master command; 5 attended/5 machine minutes; unique row/code/variant.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES; runs mc info but leaves the contradictory byte mapping to the user and uses insecure SSH.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: FULLY AUTOMATABLE/LOW once an authoritative firmware-manifest byte mapping resolves the source conflict.

old_problem: The two required byte relations are mutually ambiguous: the source neither names Firmware Revision versus Auxiliary Firmware Revision fields nor byte positions/order/encoding. A standard Get Device ID response cannot determine the OEM release-string mapping by itself.
disposition_reason: `ipmitool mc info` is a safe read-only query, but ED-03/15 prohibit guessing OEM encoding and ED-19/20 prohibit dropping either source statement. Unlike a missing IP or version value, the absent decoder is the core PASS/FAIL semantic and the original requirements conflict. The case therefore remains Pending until the BMC firmware owner supplies a field/byte/order/encoding mapping that reconciles both clauses.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2229, same-row DeepSeek columns, GPT V2, historical record, unique identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2230 / Wistron-BMC-01064-V001 / a938156a969e7b9d was directly read from XLSX and its historical record.
Preserve the literal `ipmitool mc info` read and both original byte-mapping clauses; neither may be silently discarded or reworded into an invented mapping.
The owner must name every Firmware Revision/Auxiliary Firmware Revision field and raw/rendered byte position, byte order, decimal/hex/packed encoding and canonical expected release string.
Once supplied, verify BMC device ID/GUID and run one trusted read-only mc-info query, capturing complete output, exit, timestamp and all revision fields.
A zero exit is only command completion; PASS requires deterministic manifest-backed comparison using the approved decoder.
Do not use sshpass, disable host verification, update firmware, reset BMC, mutate FRU or retry to change the result.
Standard IPMI defines Get Device ID fields but cannot resolve this platform's OEM release-string composition without the project mapping.
No login, mc-info query, firmware update, reset, retry or DUT action was executed.

test_case.test_name: BMC firmware identity from mc-info revision bytes using approved OEM mapping
test_case.purpose: Read the intended BMC's Get Device ID firmware fields and compare them to the canonical firmware release only after an authoritative mapping reconciles the source's two incompatible byte statements.
required_package: Exact SUT/BMC identity, device ID/GUID and canonical expected firmware release
Owner-approved Firmware Revision/Auxiliary Firmware Revision field/byte/order/encoding decoder reconciling both source clauses
ipmitool version and trusted protected IB or OOB access
test_case.test_command: Do not execute for verdict until the OEM decoder is approved. Then verify the controller identity, run `ipmitool mc info` once through trusted access, capture complete stdout/stderr/exit/timestamp and raw/rendered revision fields, and apply the signed manifest mapping without inference.
test_case.expected_result: The command completes without error and every mapped Firmware Revision/Auxiliary Firmware Revision byte deterministically reconstructs the approved canonical BMC firmware release under the reconciled rule.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires a signed unambiguous decoder satisfying both preserved source clauses and an exact manifest match. Shell success or visual guessing is insufficient. Until the mapping resolves the contradiction, the case remains Engineering Decision Pending; after approval, malformed data or mismatch is FAIL.
safety_gate: No execution verdict until field, byte position, byte order, encoding and expected release are signed.
Verify the exact BMC and use trusted secret-safe access.
Read-only mc-info only; no update, reset, FRU write, log clear or retry.
Stop on identity, transport, parse or mapping ambiguity.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash and BMC device identity
All Firmware Revision and Auxiliary Firmware Revision raw/rendered bytes
Signed OEM decoder reconciling both clauses, canonical expected release and comparison
test_case.recovery: No state change is expected. On identity, transport or parse failure, stop and preserve evidence; do not update/reset/retry. Semantic recovery is the owner's approved mapping, not an agent guess.

source_conflict.reason: The first-two-byte clause and first-byte-is-third-byte clause remain irreconcilable until an authority identifies their fields, positions and encoding. No approved ED resolves this case-specific OEM mapping.

blocked.reason: The read-only query is understood; the case remains Pending for its core OEM oracle rather than globally BLOCKED.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Canonical expected firmware release and authoritative Firmware Revision/Auxiliary Firmware Revision field, byte-position, order and encoding mapping reconciling both source statements; controller identity and trusted access.
pending.execution_status: ENGINEERING DECISION PENDING; CONTRADICTORY OEM VERSION-BYTE ORACLE UNRESOLVED; NO LOGIN, QUERY, UPDATE, RESET, RETRY OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED
pending.owner: BMC firmware owner and project release/configuration authority
pending.unlock_condition: Publish and approve one deterministic OEM decoder that explicitly reconciles both original clauses and maps to the canonical release string.

external_authorities.authority: IPMI Get Device ID standard behavior plus approved ED-03/ED-15/ED-19/ED-20 rules
external_authorities.application: Supports the safe read-only query but forbids inventing the OEM revision-string mapping or dropping conflicting coverage.

project_authority: BMC firmware/release owner must resolve field/byte/order/encoding semantics; end engineer owns verdict after deterministic comparison.
